content.thinking:
I need to plan out proportions for this mythic fox figure carefully before writing the whole file at once, settling on a shoulder height around 0.75m, body length 1.1m, and tails fanning up to 1.4m.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: hips as root joint, a spine chain curving from hips to chest, then a neck chain extending forward and up to the head joint. I'm keeping the API usage simple and explicit, defining parent relationships directly and building the body shape as a swept path with catmull-rom points running from the rump to the chest.

Next I'm sizing the body's elliptical cross-section — narrower at the rump, wider at the chest — and shaping the neck similarly with a slimmer sweep. I'm planning fur tufts as card-based textures for the neck, chest, cheeks, legs, and tail, then moving to head construction with a scaled sphere for the skull and a separate shape for the snout.

Now I'm working on jaw separation with its own bone, a dark nose sphere, and amber decal eyes placed on the skull surface with narrow fox-like proportions.

For ears I'm sketching a tall pointed outline with a sharp tip and mild curve, extruding it and mirroring across both sides of the head using the sign convention for left/right placement.

To avoid local-coordinate confusion, I'll decide to just position all body parts using world coordinates with bone attachments, starting from a fixed head center and building out the floor-level leg placements -- front shoulders and feet first, then moving to the hind legs.

For the hind legs I'm setting digitigrade-style hip and foot positions, then computing limb lengths and bend direction for both front and rear limbs so each chain of three joints (root, elbow, tip) reaches correctly to the foot target.

Setting up leg sweep radii and gradient coloring for the cream body with red lower sock markings...

Now I'm defining the color palette: cream for the coat, red, gold, and various blue/violet tones for flame effects, plus amber for the iris. I'm planning to apply tribal-style red markings on the flanks via SVG decals rather than full fur shading.

I'm mapping decal placements across the body—mirrored flank sweeps, shoulder marks, red paws, and facial markings like a forehead diamond and cheek stripes. Then I'm designing the nine tails as five-joint chains rooted at the rump, fanning outward and upward in a flame-like spread.

Working out each tail's azimuth and elevation angles, with center tails rising higher and outer ones lower, computing curved paths from base to tip that curl upward while keeping the lowest tails clear of the ground.

I'm tapering the tail radius profile to get a bushy base with a pointed tip, keeping the fur cream-colored with gradient shading and adding decal swirls on each tail rather than changing the base coat color.

For decal placement I'm figuring out how to orient each swirl texture against the tail's curved surface, using the sweep's hit point and tangent to set the decal's direction and up-vector so it sits flush against the tail at a chosen position along its length.

Now I'm planning the fur card scatter for the tails -- around 40 tuft cards per tail across nine tails, oriented to flow along the tail's direction toward the tip rather than following surface tangents, keeping the triangle count manageable.

For the flame effects at each tail tip, I'm setting up glowing cream-to-violet-gold cards arranged in a ring around the tip frame, angled upward with a slight bend, using a ring helper to distribute several flame cards evenly around each tip.

I'm planning to add floating spirit-flame wisp cards scattered near the body, plus small decorative elements like a gold orb at the hip and an ornate beaded collar with a hanging red tassel for extra flair.

Now I'm working out the joint budget across tails, legs, spine, neck, head, jaw, and ears, keeping it around 80 total. I'm building each tail as a chain bound to the hips, using a catmull-rom curve resampled into five joints, then skinning it with a sweep over the chain path so the tail tapers naturally from the root.

For the body, I'm figuring out how overlapping bone spans near the hips and spine1 joint get resolved -- since they sit at the same position, I'm just defaulting to the spine chain for ownership there, so the rump region behind the first spine joint deforms with spine1's rotation rather than hips.

Now I'm defining the neck chain with a short catmull path, parenting it to the last spine joint, and tapering its sweep radius. The head joint attaches at the end of the neck with a slight downward tilt, positioning the skull center and setting up where the snout will point.

I'm then placing the jaw joint under the head and building the lower jaw as a tapered rod sweeping from the chin toward the snout tip, while the upper snout gets its own tapering sweep from the brow down to the nose. I add a small dark sphere for the nose tip and leave a slight gap between upper and lower jaw to suggest a closed but visible mouth line.

Now I'm defining the skull sphere shape and scattering spiky fur tufts across the cheeks using cards that point back and sideways for volume, then placing eye decals slightly forward and to the sides of center with a defined elevation and size for a front-facing but angled gaze.

Working through the eye tilt: since the fox face is slanted rather than upright, I need to roll each eye decal — CCW rotation lifts the viewer's right side, so the left eye (positive side) gets a positive roll while the mirrored right eye gets a negative roll to keep the outer corners raised symmetrically. The red eye-line detail can just be baked into the ink decal itself rather than a separate layer.

Now I'm placing the forehead marking as a red-and-gold diamond decal positioned via a hit-test on the skull surface, then adding cheek stripe decals at symmetric azimuth angles near the jawline. For the ears, I'm extruding geometry off the head joint with an outline defined in front view and a y-direction tilted slightly outward and back so they lean naturally away from the skull.

Defining the ear outline shape with smoothing and bevel, then setting up the inner ear detail offset along the correct thickness axis for proper alignment...

Painting the ear color by height (red near tip, cream below), then setting up ear joints as hinge bones under the head so they can animate, before moving on to tail and leg decal details.

Still working out the leg markings as swirl decals projected onto the leg surface, then adding a similar flank decal placed on the body side.

Now I'm sketching the swirl texture itself as an SVG tribal design — red curling scroll paths with gold accent dots, keeping stroke widths thick enough to stay visible at the raster size. Writing swirl paths... Then I'm thinking through the body's base coloring, considering cream cel-shading with a golden-tinged back for subtle countershading.

Simplifying further, I settle on a cream-to-white fur edge for the body coat, with a subtle teeth pattern for the fur texture, and I'm now working out how to paint sock markings on the legs using a conditional based on vertical position.

For the zigzag sock edges I use a sine-like zigzag function driven by horizontal and depth coordinates, giving a jagged boundary rather than a clean line. For the tail, I decide to keep the base fur simple but gradient the color toward a cooler pale blue near the tip, sampling along the tail's path from mid-length to the very end.

Now I'm working out the collar: a gold sweep looping around the neck, picking a point along the neck's joint chain with a direction aligned to the neck's axis, and trying to generate a tight loop cut around that point on the body-neck surface, accepting there's some risk the cutting plane could miss if the neck geometry doesn't line up as expected.

Sweeping gold tube geometry along that loop, adding beaded red spheres distributed around the path, and considering a pendant orb hanging at the front lower point, while making sure the bone weights inherit properly from the neck. I'm also thinking about whether to add gold anklets on the legs using a similar loop-cutting approach around the elbow joint, though that carries similar risk of cutting in the wrong spot.

Adding anklet torus geometry...

Setting hind paw positions and tapering leg radii along the chain, checking that thigh tops still blend into the body. Now adding chest fluff and neck ruff by scattering tufted cards across the body and neck surfaces, filtered to forward-facing areas, tinted cream/gold.

Designing the tuft shape as a pointed leaf-like SVG with a cream gradient fill and a soft gold edge stroke, then planning a similar mane tuft running along the back crest.

I'm checking the overall proportions now, estimating the tail flames and curl will push the model's total height to around 1.9-2.0 units against the fox's 0.7 shoulder height, which feels acceptable for a stylized fantasy creature. I'm also sketching out the tail's base path and heading direction using trigonometric offsets from the body.

Working through tail curl geometry...

Setting up the tail chain with tapering radii and round caps, then working out decal placement along the tail using tangent direction for orientation.

Now I'm designing the flame-shaped tail markings as a dedicated SVG texture with its own viewBox, plus adding small spark and ember decorations scattered around each tail for extra flair.

Still writing flame texture paths...

Now I'm thinking about applying glow to the card meshes, and considering adding a small gold orb sphere embedded at the hip/flank area to accent the body shape.

I'm adding a thin gold ring around the orb, oriented so its axis runs along the body, then planning a hanging red-and-gold tassel beneath the collar at the chest, though I'm still working out the right placement coordinates since the loop's front point isn't precisely known.

Still placing pendant and tassel elements...

Now I'm thinking about body stripe decals using SVG textures, and whether the back mane needs a sweep path or can just be handled by scattered cards, filtering hits by position so the ruff only appears near the chest and neck while another scatter covers the hips.

Adding more scatter passes...

Checking that gradient, paint, zigzag, frame, rng, catmull, and limb helpers are all actually used so nothing gets flagged as unused, then confirming the Hit type carries proper Vector3 fields for position and normal checks. Part counts still look well within budget for decals and cards.

Setting up imports for the builder, frame, IK limb, RNG, paint/gradient, catmull paths, SVG texture, and the toon/glow kits, then starting the build function with a seeded RNG and defining the coat material using a cel-shaded fur edge effect.

Working out the sock/leg color blending with a zigzag pattern, then defining the skeleton hierarchy starting with hips as the root joint, followed by a three-segment spine chain built from catmull-rom control points, and beginning the neck chain off the spine's end joint.

Setting up the head and jaw joints with their positions and aim directions, then starting the body sweep geometry using a catmull-rom curve for the torso profile and a radius function to shape it.

Checking the chest curve values at t=0.8 to confirm the proportions land reasonably—rx comes out around .63-scaled, chest ry near .165, which looks fine for the body shape.

I'm now checking the body's vertical extent: bottom around .545, top near .875, which fits the shoulder height and leg length nicely, leaving roughly .5 of visible leg reaching the floor. I'm defining the body as a spine-bone chain colored with the coat, then sweeping the neck shape using similar coat coloring.

Now I'm working on the head geometry -- placing a skull sphere bone scaled and positioned near the top of the chest, then sweeping the snout as a tapered polyline shape from the face outward, both colored to match the fur.

Continuing with the nose details: a small dark sphere tip positioned at the end of the snout, then a lower jaw sweep with its own taper and cream coloring, plus thinking through whether to add a thin dark box for the mouth interior between the jaws.

Still placing fangs and ears, then I'm setting up skin decals using surface lookups around the head center for eyes and a forehead mark, computing hit points and orienting the decal direction against the skull's curvature.

Now I'm mirroring the cheek decal across the side and adding scattered fluff cards near the cheeks with leaning and bending for texture. Next I'm setting up the leg sweeps, looping through left and right sides to build the limb geometry symmetrically.

Still writing leg chains...

Checking reach distances for the hind limb against segment lengths confirms it works, then I move to the sweep radii and bend direction for elbows and hind knees.

Now I'm working out paw positions and toe spikes per leg, adjusting z-offsets so front and hind feet land correctly, then adding fluffy cards on the thighs, tail loops, floating wisps, and leg/flank decals.

Scattering flame-like cards along the tail surface with varied size, lean, and bend, then adding a ring of flame cards at the tail tip with upward flow and selective double-siding for the central flames.

Adding floating embers above each tip, collecting all flame meshes for a glow pass, and sketching gold wisp cards before writing everything out as template-string SVGs.

Still writing wing paths and adding gold accent strokes and eye dots, then starting a flame-shaped tailmark path for the design.

Still writing SVG shapes for the tuft, tassel, and ear details...

I'll apply a pose rotation about the z-axis to tilt each ear outward after the geometry is built, using negative degrees for the +X ear so the tip angles correctly toward the body side. Then I move on to skinning the neck and body as a connected surface before scattering fill details across it.

For the fur scatter, I'm setting different filters and densities for the chest/shoulder region versus the rear region, each with its own minimum distance threshold so the points don't crowd.

Now I'm writing the procedural tail generation loop, computing directional vectors and control points per tail segment to build curved paths...

Setting up the tail's coat gradient and shading...

I'll reuse the tail surface for both scatter and decals, and add a gold variant texture alongside the red one so I can alternate accent marks by position and side for variety.

Now I need thin whisker rods extending from the muzzle sides and small red eyebrow tube sweeps positioned just above the eyes against the skull curvature.

Checking the math, the eyebrow points fall outside the skull ellipsoid, so they'd float unnaturally -- I'll skip those and rely on the decal eyes plus forehead mark instead. For the neck, I'm setting up a loop attachment on the neck surface at a point along its sweep path, roughly where the neck axis curves midway between shoulders and jaw.

Now I'm sketching the collar: sweeping a gold band along the neck loop, then scattering nine small red beads around it using a path-following helper, placing each bead at a frame along the loop. For the pendant, I'm finding the nearest point on the body/neck surface to a target position and sticking a small gold sphere there with a slight embed, possibly adding a glow effect.

Still placing details...

I'm also laying out tassel cards hanging down from the pendant point, flipping their orientation and giving them a downward flow with a thin, elongated size. Then I'm defining eight scattered wisp positions around the figure, each one set up to attach to its nearest joint since they're not tied to any specific bone, and the floating cards follow the same nearest-joint fallback logic. Now I'm thinking through how the floor contact should be handled.

Still placing surface decals...

I'm positioning swirl and leg-mark decals on the thighs and front legs with mirrored x-offsets so the artwork reads correctly from outside the body, and I'm adding flank and shoulder swirl decals with matching mirroring, while considering whether to swap in a hip orb on the flank instead.

I'm checking that the glow helper works correctly on mesh arrays, confirming the TypeScript typings for frame cards and the rng callback, and now writing the ear generation logic with extrusion thickness options.

Still writing paint colors...

I'm reviewing other potential typecheck issues: limb path returns, chain sweep options, and the sides property.

Setting up the eye texture parameters and double-checking which helper functions like paint and gradient are actually used versus imported unnecessarily. I'm also verifying that the tail sweep's point-at-parameter call correctly exposes a tangent getter.

Confirming the spike helper's argument order with direction vectors, radius, and color options, and planning how to attach flame card decals along the ring. The tuft on the tail and the body's gradient-based paint variations per tail look fine, so I'm ready to write the file.
